interface.title: ΨDataViz (PsiDataViz): Scientific Data Visualization
interface.field: Analytical and physical chemistry / materials characterization: DSC, FTIR, Raman, NMR, XRD and more
interface.stage_of_work: Data management and first-look visualization of raw instrument files, then format conversion and export for downstream analysis
interface.what_it_is_for: Point it at public data folders or upload local instrument files; it sorts them into datasets by technique, overlays and normalizes spectra or thermograms across techniques, lets you edit sample metadata, and exports to standard formats or a reproducible notebook.

data.note: All 9 test files were uploaded through 'Choose files / zip' on the Ψ|Data⟩ (DATA) tab and became 8 datasets (DSC 4, FTIR 1, NMR 2, Raman 1); the Agilent .jdx and .txt were grouped into one dataset. The test files are trimmed, so DSC and FTIR show only the ends of each segment. Contrary to the brief, the network did work for GitHub: clicking Quick add 'yargerlab/Data' on the DATA tab finished after a minute or two and added 8,039 remote datasets, and remote files loaded in full. The full acetaminophen DSC, indium DSC, CBD Raman and CBD FTIR results come from that remote source. A scan of the same repository from the QUICK tab never finished (screens/040.webp). PubChem name lookup failed; SMILES-based structure rendering worked.

features.name: Local folder/zip drop zone with automatic technique classification
features.general: Drop a set of raw instrument files and get them grouped into datasets labelled by measurement type, with counts per type
features.specific: 'Drag a folder or .zip here' / Choose folder / Choose files / zip; files are parsed in memory into a 'Local upload · N files' source and technique chips (DSC 4, FTIR 1, NMR 2, Raman 1); files of one measurement in two formats are grouped into one row (.jdx, .txt)
steps: Press Choose files / zip (or Choose folder, or drag)
Select the instrument files
Read the source chip and per-technique counts
Remove the source with × on its chip if needed
serves_tasks: Load local files and let the tool sort them into datasets by technique

features.name: Public-repository quick add
features.general: Pull the file listing of a public online data repository into the same catalog as local files, classified by measurement type
features.specific: Quick add preset buttons on the Ψ|Data⟩ tab (used: GH yargerlab/Data); shows 'Scanning https://github.com/yargerlab/Data …', then a 'yargerlab/Data 8039' source chip, '8,047 datasets across 2 sources' and 18 technique chips
steps: Press a Quick add preset
Wait for the 'Scanning …' message to finish
Read the new source chip count and technique chips
serves_tasks: Add a public online data repository as another source alongside local files

features.name: Catalog filtering by technique and free text
features.general: Narrow a combined table of datasets by measurement type and by a sample keyword, then pick rows to plot
features.specific: PsiData panel: single-select technique chips and 'filter by sample, date…'; the header reads 'N of M datasets — click to overlay'
steps: Click a technique chip
Type a sample keyword in the filter box
Click rows to send them to the plot
serves_tasks: Narrow the catalog to one technique

features.name: Click-to-overlay spectrum/thermogram plot with normalization and draw modes
features.general: Toggle table rows on and off a shared plot; each row adds one trace per segment or accumulation; normalize to compare shapes across instruments; switch draw style
features.specific: PsiViz: clicking a dataset row adds or removes it ('N datasets overlaid'); DSC splits into ramp segments, Raman into accumulations, 2D NMR into F1 rows; NMR datasets go on per-nucleus tabs; Normalize rescales each trace to 0–1; Line / Points / Line + points; NMR and FTIR axes are reversed; Clear empties the plot
steps: Click one or more rows in the dataset table
Tick Normalize to compare different-intensity techniques
Choose Line, Points or Line + points
Press Clear to start over
serves_tasks: Overlay spectra of the same compound from two techniques to compare bands
Inspect a thermal curve over repeated heat-cool cycles for melting and glass-transition features
Inspect a 1D NMR spectrum and a 2D NMR dataset
Explore and capture the plot: change trace style and scaling, hide traces, zoom into a region, and save an image

features.name: Interactive chart exploration (zoom, legend toggles, hover readout, PNG)
features.general: Zoom into a feature with a box, hide or isolate traces from the legend, read exact x/y values by hovering, and save the view as an image
features.specific: Standard Plotly toolbar and legend: box-zoom drag, double-click reset, Autoscale/Home, legend click hides a trace (hint: 'Double-click on legend to isolate one trace'), hover tooltip shows (158.58, 1.297), camera downloads newplot.png ('Snapshot succeeded')
steps: Drag a box over the region of interest
Click legend entries to hide traces
Hover a peak to read its coordinates
Double-click to reset and press the camera to save
serves_tasks: Explore and capture the plot: change trace style and scaling, hide traces, zoom into a region, and save an image
Compare a reference standard's melting and freezing peaks and read off peak values

features.name: Per-dataset metadata editor with categorized tags
features.general: Review metadata read from the file, fill in missing sample/instrument/condition fields, and add categorized tags that travel with the data
features.specific: Sample & metadata panel (one per overlaid dataset): Sample name, Instrument, Operator, Date, Time, Solvent, Temperature, Pressure, Notes; Chemical identity with Identify (SMILES → 2D structure, fills SMILES); tags typed Condition/Instrument/Chemical via + Tag; edits are picked up by 'Export with this metadata'
steps: Overlay a dataset to open its metadata panel
Edit fields such as Solvent, Temperature and Notes
Choose a tag category, type a value, press + Tag
Optionally Identify the compound from a SMILES
serves_tasks: Edit sample, instrument and condition metadata and add categorized tags
Identify the chemical from a structure string

features.name: Technique-aware format converter
features.general: Download a parsed dataset in a choice of interchange formats, with the formats suited to its technique flagged as recommended and the edited metadata embedded
features.specific: Export ▾ menu: 'Recommended for DSC/NMR' JCAMP-DX (.jdx) and CSDM (.csdf), then Other formats HDF5 (.h5), CSV — tidy, Parquet, Feather; the CSDM file carried the edited solvent, temperature, notes and tags under application.com.psidataviz
steps: Select a dataset in the plot
Open Export ▾
Pick a recommended or other format
Read or download the file
serves_tasks: Convert a dataset to a standard interchange format with the edited metadata embedded

features.name: Reproducible-notebook export
features.general: Generate a notebook that re-fetches and re-plots exactly the datasets currently overlaid
features.specific: Open in… ▾ → Colab / Jupyter (.ipynb) or marimo (.py): psidata_export with a DATASETS list, X_QUANTITY temperature/time, and a Plotly overlay with reversed axis for NMR/FTIR
steps: Overlay the datasets to reproduce
Open Open in… ▾
Pick Colab/Jupyter or marimo
Upload the notebook to Colab or run marimo edit --sandbox
serves_tasks: Export a notebook that reproduces loading and plotting the selected datasets
